title: Recovery of affine fan morphisms on points and basic sections
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space with a sheaf $\mathcal A$ of commutative monoids with sharp stalks, and let $P$ be a fine sharp monoid. Put $S(P)=(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P,\overline{\mathcal M}_P)$, with the spectrum and local-morphism conventions of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. For a morphism $g:(T,\mathcal A)\to S(P)$ with local stalk maps, let $\varphi_g:P\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal A)$ be pullback of canonical sections. Then for every $x\in T$ and $p\in P$ one has $\varphi_g(p)_x=0$ if and only if $p\notin g(x)$, and consequently $g(x)=\{p:\varphi_g(p)_x\ne0\}$. For every $a\in P$, using the canonical identification $\Gamma(D(a),\overline{\mathcal M}_P)=P_a/P_a^\times$ of [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections], the class $\operatorname{cl}(p-na)$ equals $\operatorname{cl}(p)$ and its pullback by $g$ is $\varphi_g(p)|_{g^{-1}D(a)}$. These prescribed maps on basic opens uniquely determine the sheaf map on all opens. In particular, if $g'$ is a second local morphism from $(T,\mathcal A)$ to $S(P)$ and $\varphi_{g'}=\varphi_g$, then $g'=g$ as morphisms, including both their point maps and their sheaf maps.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.1.8(ii) and proof using (i), printed p.99: uniqueness of the local factorization and the section correspondence; 3.1.3--3.1.6, pp.98--99. Expands old parent Steps 5--6 (recovery). No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric assertion.

proof.text: Fix $x\in T$ and put $\mathfrak p=g(x)$. By the stalk-map and canonical-section definitions [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], $\varphi_g(p)_x=g_x^\#(\operatorname{cl}(p))$. The target stalk is sharp. The source stalk is $P_{\mathfrak p}/P_{\mathfrak p}^\times$ by [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections] and is sharp too: if classes of $u,v$ sum to zero, $u+v$ is a unit, so an inverse $w$ of $u+v$ makes $v+w$ an inverse of $u$; thus $\operatorname{cl}(u)=0$. Locality therefore says that $g_x^\#(\operatorname{cl}(p))=0$ exactly when $\operatorname{cl}(p)=0$. The final clause of the localization lemma makes this equivalent to $p\notin\mathfrak p$. Taking complements recovers $g(x)=\{p:\varphi_g(p)_x\ne0\}$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.5--3.1.8, printed p.99; point recovery by locality and 3.1.3--3.1.4 stalk calculation.

proof.text: Fix $a,p\in P$ and $n\in\mathbf N$. In $P_a=P-\mathbf N a$, both $na$ and $-na$ belong to $P_a$ and are inverses. Hence $\operatorname{cl}(p-na)=\operatorname{cl}(p)$ by the sharpening definition [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. By [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections], restriction of the canonical global section $p$ to $D(a)$ is exactly $\operatorname{cl}(p)$. Compatibility of the sheaf map with restriction now gives $g_{D(a)}^\#(\operatorname{cl}(p-na))=\varphi_g(p)|_{g^{-1}D(a)}$. Every element of $P_a$ has the displayed form, so this specifies the map on every basic-open section.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.3, printed p.98, and uniqueness in 3.1.8(ii), p.99; denominator classes and restriction.

proof.text: For a fixed point map, let two sheaf maps have the same components on all $D(a)$. If $U$ is open and $s\in\overline{\mathcal M}_P(U)$, naturality identifies the restrictions of its two pullbacks to $g^{-1}D(a)$ with the common basic-open pullback of $s|_{D(a)}$, for every $D(a)\subseteq U$. The basic opens form a basis by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], so these inverse images cover $g^{-1}U$. The injectivity of the first map in the sheaf equalizer [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, clause (1)] says the two pullbacks are equal. This proves uniqueness of every open component, including the empty open, whose sheaf of sections has one element.

source.place: VIII 3.1.3--3.1.4(iii), p.98, and 3.1.8, p.99; explicit sheaf separation on the basic-open cover.

proof.text: If $\varphi_{g'}=\varphi_g$, their germs are equal for every $p,x$. Step 1 gives equality of the image primes for each $x$, hence equality of the continuous maps. Under that equality, Step 2 gives equality of every basic-open sheaf component, since its value on each class is the same restricted canonical pullback. Step 3 gives equality on every open. Thus both pieces of the morphism data agree, and $g'=g$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NC-29381e234 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Ordinary first split with no new nodes; live and side-live both still have the item unsplit with an identical statement, and there is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply. I checked the source at ILO VIII 3.1.5-3.1.6 and Lemma 3.1.8(i)/(ii) with its proof, printed p.99. The source defines f(x)=P minus phi_x^{-1}(units) and calls the rest 'straightforward'; the item writes out that uniqueness half, and with sharp stalks the source's point map matches the item's formula. Step 1: the stalk map applied to the canonical germ, with both stalks sharp; the proof that the source stalk P_p/P_p^x is sharp is checked. Locality h^{-1}(0)=0 plus the last clause of lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections gives zero germ iff p is not in g(x). Step 2: cl(p-na)=cl(p) because na and -na are mutually inverse in P_a; restriction of the canonical section to D(a) is cl(p) by the localization lemma, and naturality gives the basic component. Step 3, elementary: the equalizer from clause (1) of def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology on the cover by g^{-1}D(a), using D(a) meet D(b) = D(a+b); the empty open is covered. Step 4 compares point maps before sheaf maps. Cited statements say what each step uses (C3/C4), proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no cycle (the parent hom-universal is not cited; the closure of the cited nodes does not contain the item), and there is no off-route statement: the sites node is a definition. Small cases P={0}, N and <2,3>, empty T and empty opens, and the need for locality were all checked. Mathlib searches cover all three kinds. No fixes.
